subject: Field kickoff readiness kit, hands-on workshop & calendar sync
messages:
From: Joe Turner <joe.turner@acme-cloud.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: platform-eng@acme-cloud.com
Date: 2027-05-24T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Field kickoff: hands-on workshop + load test prep

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed. We want to move to a hands-on kickoff where we:
- walk through prompt templates and routing rules for multitenant decks
- run a short load test to validate tail latency at 4k tokens
- validate KV-cache behavior across session continuity

We are targetting a 3-hour working session with engineers and product folks. Proposed windows:
- Tue Jun 8, 9:00–12:00 PT
- Thu Jun 10, 10:00–13:00 PT

Can you confirm availability and send a short prep pack (agenda + checklist + any sandbox access notes)? Also please call out what we should pre-run on our side (data subsets, prompt sets).

Attendees from our side: Joe Turner (Eng manager), Sarah Lin (Product), platform-eng@acme-cloud.com (infra alias).

Thanks,
Joe Turner
Director, Cloud Integrations
Acme Cloud

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Joe Turner <joe.turner@acme-cloud.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-24T16:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Field kickoff: hands-on workshop + load test prep

Hi Joe — great to hear. Both slots are possible on our side; we prefer Thu Jun 10 to give engineering a bit more runway to prep.

Quick checklist of what we'll distribute as a prep pack:
- One-page agenda (what we will accomplish hour-by-hour) [workshop_agenda_v1.pdf]
- Hands-on checklist (environment access, prompt review items, sample datasets) [hands_on_checklist.xlsx]
- Sandbox access instructions + temporary API keys (expires after workshop)
- Suggested prompt set + routing matrix to review before session
- Short load-test plan and metrics we will collect (tail latency, p50/p95/p99, token cost)

Marissa, can you draft the agenda and own the invite? Dev — can you prepare the load-test plan and confirm expected GPU profile?

Joe — if Jun 10 works we will lock it and send invites + pre-reads by EOD tomorrow.

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_prep_brief.md (MD)]

From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@acme-cloud.com>

On Tue, May 25, 2027 at 09:14 AM, Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@acme-cloud.com> wrote:

Thanks, Karthik. Jun 10 is close — we have a leadership review that morning and need to push one day. Would Jun 11, 11:00–14:00 PT work instead?

Quick asks from our side for the prep pack:
- A short list of 6–8 prep questions we can circulate internally (e.g., "what are our priority prompt patterns?", "expected QPS per tenant?").
- A small sample dataset (anonymized) or instructions to subset ours.
- Any RBAC details—who needs sandbox keys vs view-only links.

We also want the agenda to include a 30-min slot for routing discussion (how we want rules to map to model variants).

Joe and I will confirm final attendees tomorrow.

— Sarah
Sarah Lin
Product Lead, Acme Cloud

Marissa / Dev / Laura — locking Jun 11, 11:00–14:00 PT per Acme ask. Please see below for owners and assets to publish. I copied the exact asks from Acme so nothing gets missed.

Agenda (draft — hour blocks):
- 11:00–11:15: Introductions & objectives (Karthik)
- 11:15–12:00: Prompt review + routing patterns (Karthik + Sarah)
- 12:00–12:30: Hands-on build: sample prompt flows (Marissa leads)
- 12:30–13:00: Load test prep & run (Dev leads)
- 13:00–13:30: Inspect metrics & tail latency analysis
- 13:30–14:00: Action items & rollout next steps (Laura + Marissa)

Assets to publish (owners):
- workshop_agenda_v1.pdf — Marissa (owner: marissa_cole)
- hands_on_checklist.xlsx — Marissa
- redwood_prep_brief.md — Karthik (includes sandbox key instructions)
- acme_test_plan_v0.3.docx — Dev (load test infra & commands)

Prep questions (we'll include these in the mail):
1) Which prompt templates are critical vs experimental for this workshop?
2) Expected QPS (steady-state) and peak bursts for a single tenant?
3) Any tokens-per-request limits we should plan against?
4) Which parts of the flow require state continuity (KV cache) vs stateless?
5) Are partners/tools (vector DB / rerankers) in the loop?
6) Who will own acceptance criteria for performance?

Links: https://drive.redwood.company/shared/ACME/kickoff-readiness (I'll publish the files here)

Attachments: workshop_agenda_v1.pdf, hands_on_checklist.xlsx, acme_test_plan_v0.3.docx

Joe / Sarah — we'll send the official invite and the prep pack by EOD tomorrow; please confirm the attendee list once you have it.

Thanks — K
